verdict.rationale: Claude ships official desktop apps, including Linux installation via an apt repository. Its Cowork computer-use feature can work directly on the user's screen by clicking, typing and opening apps, which covers screen access. Nothing in the evidence documents OS-level or global keyboard shortcuts, so only part of the story is delivered. Missing for 10: documented OS-level/global hotkeys, explicit confirmation that screen access runs in the desktop app, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can use an official desktop app with OS-level shortcuts and access to what is on my screen

citations.quote: The Claude desktop apps bring Claude's capabilities directly to your computer, allowing for seamless integration with your workflow.
you can install Claude Desktop from Anthropic's apt repository rather than as a downloaded .deb file
When computer use is enabled and Claude doesn't have a connector or tool for what you need, it may navigate to your screen directly—clicking, typing, and opening apps just like you would.
